featured_reviews.review_text:
*Please go for 2nd-3rd opinion*

We consulted Dr Carlton Perreault at Surya Hospital for my 11-month-old son, who had suffered from frequent ear infections (at least three episodes). Our general physician had suggested that we consult an ENT specialist to rule out the need for grommet insertion (myringotomy), if required.

From the beginning, the consultation felt uncomfortable. Dr. Carlton spent considerable time asking about our background and whereabouts probably coz of my wife's accent. When my wife mentioned that we live in Australia and were visiting India for family function and partly because appointments and procedures can be done quicker here, his attitude noticeably changed.

Dr. Carlton then recommended two diagnostic tests for our 11-month-old baby and also suggested a specific diagnostic center. This raised concerns for us. When we checked with multiple other reputed diagnostic centres, they were surprised by these tests being advised for such a young baby and mentioned that these tests are extremely difficult to perform on infants, as the child must remain still for several minutes. We were told by more than one center that these tests are rarely done on babies of this age.

Despite the tests being practically inconclusive, the diagnostic center contacted the doctor, and the results were presented in a way that made it seem like surgery was urgently required.

Dr Carlton explained the condition and the surgical procedure in detail, but at the same time created a sense of urgency and fear, stating that if we delayed the decision, our child could potentially lose his hearing. We requested a few days as we had to travel to our native place. He prescribed antibiotics and pain medication and asked us to decide quickly.

After returning a week later, we sought second opinions from *three senior pediatric ENT specialists* at reputed hospitals. All of them were shocked that such tests were recommended for an infant and strongly disagreed with the suggestion of surgery. They performed a proper examination using an endoscopic camera to inspect the ear canal and eardrum. Their conclusion was consistent: there was only some ear wax, the ears looked healthy, and **no surgery was required at all**.

Based on our experience, I felt extremely uncomfortable and disappointed. It seemed like unnecessary tests and a surgical procedure were being pushed on us, which could have been avoided entirely.

I strongly request parents consulting Dr Carlton to **please seek a second or even third opinion**, especially before agreeing to any surgery for a child.
